common.text: Somebody just walked out hungry. Don't let them wait! A hungry guest tells ten friends.
Your rating is slipping. Keep the counter stocked, or hire a waiter to help.
See that glowing tree? Old timber like that is worth a fortune. Chop it before it fades!
Big upgrades take time. The place keeps running while the builders work. Come back when it's done.
Here comes a crowd! Keep the food flowing and nobody leaves.
The line is full, so new guests are walking past. More fires, more upgrades, more help!

beats.text: Forty years I've fed hikers on this trail. My back's done, so the camp is yours now. Here's my axe.
Chop wood, keep the fire going, serve the hungry ones. Grayline Lumber wants this forest. Don't give it to them.
Ranger Doyle. Grayline says nobody uses this trail. If your camp brings in the crowds, I can protect it.
Victor Grayline. Cute little camp. My survey crew is marking these trees. Sell me the lot before winter.
That lad used to cut for Grayline until they laid him off. Treat your crew well and they'll do the same for you.
The Trail Festival is coming! Feed the crowd well and I'll have the proof I need to protect this forest.
The trail is protected! Here's a road permit. There's an empty shack out on the highway...
I knew you had it in you. Go on, the highway is waiting. Your crew will keep the camp going.
Too many hikers left hungry. Get the kitchen ready, then try again.
A shack on the highway! Grayline trucks run this road all day, and their drivers eat out of vending machines.
Name's Rosa. I've driven this road twenty years. Make a burger worth stopping for and every trucker will follow me.
A drive-thru window! Now we don't even have to park. Cars pay by card, and pay well.
My billboard says 'Next food: 80 miles. Grayline Stop.' Your little shack is ruining my numbers.
Good, more hands. The convoy is coming soon, and you'll need every one of them.
I've called the whole convoy. Twelve rigs, all hungry. Ready when you are!
Every driver on this road knows your name now. Grayline's mill on the lake pays nothing. Finn's free mill across the water pays real money.
Half the convoy drove off hungry. Stock up and call me again.
I'm Finn. Grayline owns the near mill and pays pennies for logs. Raft them over to my mill and I'll pay three times as much.
Anglers are patient folk, but they eat a lot. Keep the fryers busy.
Fine raft! Load her up and she'll sail to my mill. That timber keeps my saws turning for another week.
Fine. Grayline now pays double for logs. ...Still less than Finn? Ridiculous.
The fishing tournament is here. Every angler on the lake wants a feast!
My mill is safe, thanks to you. There's a lodge up the mountain, freezing since Grayline cut the windbreak.
The anglers went home grumbling. Get more fish in the fryer and try again.
Ingrid, ski school. Grayline cut the windbreak forest and now the lodge is an icebox. Warm it up and I'll bring every class I teach.
Cold guests don't wait. A fire in the hearth changes everything.
A real fire! Keep it fed and the skiers will stay, and pay more for the comfort.
You're planting trees where I cut them? That's... bad for business. Mine, I mean.
A blizzard is rolling in and every skier is coming down at once. Keep that fire burning!
Warmest lodge on the mountain! The harvest fair committee wants you, and Grayline has bought a stand there too.
They froze and left. Stack the fireplace full before the next storm.
Judge Hollis, fair committee. The best stand at the fair wins the valley's blessing. Grayline has a stand right across from yours.
May the best stand win. It'll be mine. Long lines? My stand takes your guests.
The fair bell! Ring it and the whole fair comes running. Double prices while the rush lasts.
Don't race him on price. Beat him on service.
Judging day. Every guest you lose walks across to Grayline's stand. Show us what you've got!
Best stand at the fair, by a mile! Grayline is losing money everywhere. His Grand Timber Hotel is up for sale.
Ha! They came to my stand instead. Better luck next year.
Mr. Bell, concierge. I stayed through every bad year Grayline gave this hotel. Welcome home. Your grandmother worked here as a girl.
The Grand Timber! Bring her back to life. And watch the VIPs: they pay three times as much, but they don't like waiting.
Room service is back! Load the van and the whole valley eats hotel steak.
Last offer. Give me back the old camp and I'll leave this hotel alone. ...No? Then you'll see.
The critic has arrived, with her VIP party. Her review decides everything.
Five stars! Grayline has sold his last holdings and left the valley. The empire is yours.
Look at all this. You did it the right way. There are other valleys where Grayline still operates...
The critic left early. We'll invite her again once we're ready.
